findings.claim: The fallback archives whatever active memory holds the derived key '<key>/part-i', and it no longer checks the title. If the document's part i is no longer active (user-archived or superseded) and an unrelated memory has since taken '<key>/part-i', a shorter re-save archives that unrelated memory. The previous commit's title guard prevented this. The archive is reversible (status='archived', not deleted). No test covers a non-moved holder with an unrelated title.
proof_refs: internal/memory/save.go:243-263 (oldParts comes only from part 1's title, so part i can be absent while oldParts >= i)

findings.claim: (a) A part moved to '<key>/part-i~n' and then renamed with mem_update matches neither query and stays active after a shorter re-save. (b) When such a renamed moved part coexists with an unrelated memory holding '<key>/part-i', the moved query finds nothing and the fallback archives the unrelated holder. Both need an importer-moved key plus a rename.
proof_refs: internal/memory/import.go:197-208 (the importer moves a part to '<key>~N')
